Open an app to run R in your browser. The first launch downloads R and the
required packages. The [Shiny walkthrough](shiny.html) explains the code behind
the examples.

```{r gallery, echo=FALSE}
library(htmltools)

card <- function(app, title, description) {
  tags$div(
    class = "col",
    tags$a(
      class = "card h-100 text-decoration-none text-body",
      href = paste0("../live/", app, "/index.html"),
      tags$img(
        class = "card-img-top",
        src = paste0("../shiny-gallery/", app, ".webp"),
        alt = ""
      ),
      tags$div(
        class = "card-body",
        tags$h2(class = "h5 mt-0 mb-2", title),
        tags$p(class = "mb-0", description)
      )
    )
  )
}

tags$div(
  class = "shiny-gallery row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-2 g-3",
  card(
    "basic",
    "Iris explorer",
    "Switch between sepal and petal measurements for 150 flowers."
  ),
  card(
    "proxy",
    "Air passengers",
    "Add a month and switch between a line and columns using a Shiny proxy."
  ),
  card(
    "events",
    "Equalizer",
    "Select a frequency and drag its point to change the gain in decibels."
  ),
  card(
    "linked",
    "Linked charts",
    "Click a species to explore its individual flowers in a second chart."
  ),
  card(
    "stock",
    "Stock prices",
    "Zoom from weekly SPY closes to daily prices for the selected dates."
  )
)
```
